key_insight: A modular concert-editing framework combines musical activity, visual quality and beat timing to choose camera views. Its interpretable scoring makes those choices easier to inspect, although the supplied abstract reports mixed exploratory findings.
problem_solved: Editing multi-camera concerts requires choosing views that show musically relevant performers, maintain image quality and cut at appropriate musical moments.
method: Combine instrument activity from multitrack audio with visible-instrument information and image sharpness.
Use beat-based timing and probabilistic camera selection, guided by an interpretable score over complete shot intervals.
Evaluate components and conduct an exploratory expert study using a four-camera concert.
impact: The framework illustrates how audio and visual signals can support interpretable creative automation. For practitioners, it offers a modular design to investigate rather than evidence of consistently superior editing.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multitrack audio and camera footage → feature scores → camera selection → edited concert.
Beat-aligned timeline showing instrument activity, shot intervals and camera changes.
Four-camera comparison grid annotated with visible instruments and sharpness scores.
Score breakdown showing how musical relevance and visual quality influence a selected view.
paper_title: Multimodal Concert Video Editing: System Design and Exploratory Evaluation
paper_authors: Lennart Schiweck, Adrian Kempf, Michelle Retig, Moritz Feucht, Tim Mangliers
